plan: predicting shared blind spots from the models themselves
written: 2026-09-26, before any representation similarity was computed
status: exploratory; outcome data (EyePACS confirmation set) previously opened under lock v3
question: Can properties of the models, measured without disease labels, predict how often two models miss the same eyes?
pairs: 36 pairs of different variants (plus 9 seed-sibling pairs for the variance-components model)

observed_targets.primary: latent (tetrachoric) correlation of referable-disease misses at 25% referral, seed-averaged
secondary: co-miss ratio for grade 3 or worse

predictors.P1_disagreement_identity: P(both wrong) = (pA + pB - D)/2, with error rates pA, pB taken from one random half of the confirmation set (labels) and disagreement D from the other half (no labels); compared with the actual joint error on the second half
predictors.P2_pretrained_CKA: linear CKA between pretrained backbones (before any retinal training) on 2,000 unlabelled confirmation-set images; transformers mean-pooled
predictors.P3_finetuned_CKA: linear CKA between the trained models' penultimate features (seed 0) on the same images
predictors.P4_structural_similarity: count of shared attributes: family (CNN or transformer), exact architecture, pretraining data, pretraining objective

analyses.primary: Spearman correlation across the 36 pairs between each of P2, P3, P4 and the primary target, with intervals from resampling variants (1,000)
analyses.P1: mean absolute and relative error of the predicted joint error rate across pairs
analyses.variance_components: regression of the latent correlation on indicators of shared architecture, shared pretraining data, shared objective and seed-sibling status; the intercept estimates the floor that no difference among these removes

what_counts_as_a_signal: P2 (pretrained CKA) correlating positively with the primary target with an interval excluding zero would mean complementarity can be anticipated before any training on retinal images
caveats: all models trained on the same EyePACS data, so the data term cannot be estimated here
CKA measures representation similarity, not decision similarity
